records.name: Abscopal effect
records.tldr: An abscopal response is regression outside an irradiated area, studied as a possible systemic effect of local radiation. Observing it does not by itself establish the cause or an added survival benefit.
records.summary:
Responses at non-irradiated sites motivate investigation of immune effects of local radiation. Keep the irradiated and unirradiated lesions, other treatments and observation times explicit. A proposed immune mechanism needs more than local injury or circulating markers.

A case or uncontrolled combination cannot isolate the added effect of radiation. Comparative local-treatment studies must retain their populations and endpoints: a response outside the field, progression-free survival, overall survival and symptom relief are different outcomes.

notes: First define the irradiated field and the actual exposure of each lesion. A local response does not demonstrate a distant response. An uninjected-lesion response in an injection study is a different route-defined observation. During concurrent systemic treatment, distant shrinkage does not by itself isolate radiation’s contribution or demonstrate immune causation; local control, distant response, survival, symptoms and harms require separate assessment.

Demaria’s bilateral 67NR mammary-tumour mouse experiment combined local radiation with Flt3 ligand. The distant tumour grew more slowly under the combination, whereas radiation alone affected the irradiated tumour; antigen-mismatched and T-cell-deficient comparisons supported an immune-dependent component. This is a defined combined animal intervention, not a human response rate. Postow’s ipilimumab-plus-radiation melanoma report was one case with temporal immune correlates, not a study of frequency.

Formenti enrolled 39 people with chemotherapy-refractory metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer in a single-arm radiation-plus-ipilimumab study. At day 88, 21 had completed treatment and response assessment. Seven responses were 7/39, about 18% of those enrolled, or 7/21, about 33% of those evaluable. Seventeen received fewer than four cycles because they progressed or died before day 88; another completed four cycles without response assessment. These denominators answer different questions and neither estimates radiation-alone activity or an individual breast-cancer response probability.

To assess a distant effect, retain lesion exposure, serial imaging, prespecified response rules, timing and concurrent therapies. Report lesion changes separately from patient response proportions and their eligible denominators. Imaging is an input; optional tissue and immune tests use finite samples. Exposure misclassification, missing assessments, selected evaluable groups and concurrent-drug attribution can distort interpretation. There is no universal abscopal cutoff or percentage across cancers and regimens; case observations, model mechanisms and comparative clinical outcomes are different evidence tiers.

In a fictional combination study, an irradiated site is controlled while a lesion outside the field shrinks during systemic therapy. The observation is a distant response under that treatment context. It does not prove that radiation vaccinated the whole body, establish which component caused it or supply a general response frequency. Test exposure, relevant comparisons and the proposed immune mechanism separately.

Ho's single-arm phase 2 study combined radiation with pembrolizumab in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The week-13 unirradiated-lesion endpoint yielded three responses among seventeen enrolled people, 17.6%, with a 95% confidence interval of 4.7% to 44.2%. Eight died from progression before week 13; among the nine assessed then, the same three responses were 33.3%, rounded to one decimal place. These are different denominators for the same numerator, not two treatment effects. Without a randomised systemic-treatment-only group, neither proportion estimates what radiation added or supplies a general abscopal probability.

records.name: Antigen-processing machinery (APM)
records.tldr: Cells cut up proteins, move some fragments to a loading site and place them on display molecules that T cells can inspect. Having a protein inside a cell does not guarantee its fragment is shown.
records.summary:
Antigen-processing machinery (APM) is the set of proteins that generate, transport and load peptides onto HLA. A common class I route has five steps. (1) The proteasome cuts intracellular proteins into fragments, which can create a useful peptide or destroy it. (2) The transporter associated with antigen processing, TAP1 with TAP2, moves peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum; Shepherd et al. (1993) showed in a cell-free system that TAP1 is part of an ATP-dependent, sequence-selective peptide translocator. (3) ERAP1 and ERAP2 trim amino acids from the front end. York et al. (2002) found that ERAP1 can enhance or limit presentation by trimming epitopes to 8 to 9 residues, and Saveanu et al. (2005) found complementary human ERAP1 and ERAP2 activity, so more expression does not universally improve display. A class I HLA heavy chain assembles with beta-2 microglobulin (B2M) and a peptide, with helpers such as tapasin. (4) Stable peptide-HLA complexes reach the surface; the peptide stays held by HLA. (5) A compatible T-cell receptor on a conventional CD8 T cell may recognise the pair; recognition is a separate gate and display alone does not show killing.

Class II HLA commonly loads peptides in vesicles that process acquired proteins. An invariant chain protects the new groove and directs it there; after cutting, a remaining fragment is exchanged for other peptides with help from HLA-DM, and conventional CD4 T cells inspect these displays. Cross-presentation lets externally acquired material reach class I. The scheme is a common route, not a rule for every peptide.

A cancer cell may keep an altered protein and still show little of its peptide, and a shared processing defect can affect several targets at once, so adding candidate peptides does not bypass the bottleneck. Low expression, gene loss and a functional defect are different findings: a weak RNA signal does not prove deletion. Interferon gamma can increase presentation machinery when its signalling pathway and the required genes are intact, and cannot replace a deleted B2M or HLA gene. Sucker et al. (2017) described melanoma lesions in which JAK1 or JAK2 defects gave interferon-gamma resistance and evolved into HLA class I negative, T-cell-resistant lesions with antigen-presentation genes silenced and no longer inducible. Zaretsky et al. (2016) found, in biopsies from patients with acquired resistance to PD-1 blockade, JAK1 or JAK2 loss of function in two of four patients and a truncating B2M mutation with lost surface class I in a third. These are melanoma observations, not treatment-benefit evidence.

Evidence layers differ. DNA sequence and copy number show gene retention or alteration but not expression or function; RNA shows sampled gene activity but not protein, assembly or display; protein staining or flow cytometry detects protein but not which peptide is shown; HLA-associated peptide recovery shows a peptide was recovered with HLA in that preparation but not its cell of origin or recognition; controlled T-cell recognition shows function against tested targets. Peptide loading can bypass processing, so rescue by supplied peptide supports a bottleneck under those conditions only. Binding prediction is not presentation, and CD4 help is not proof of CD8 tumour recognition.

B2M-dependent assembly, loss of a restricting HLA allele and an inducible signalling defect are different dependencies. records.name: Biologically effective dose (BED) and EQD2
records.tldr: Biologically effective dose compares radiation patterns under a stated model and tissue assumption. It does not establish equal clinical outcomes or safety.
records.summary:
Biologically effective dose, or BED, is calculated from a radiation pattern and a specified tissue-and-endpoint model. In the basic equal-fraction linear-quadratic calculation, both total dose and dose per fraction matter, together with the assumed alpha/beta ratio. The result is a modelled quantity reported in gray, not extra physical dose.

EQD2 expresses the dose in two-gray fractions that would give the same modelled effect under the same assumptions. Neither expression is a universal conversion between any schedules. Repair, time, distribution and model validity must be considered for the actual irradiation pattern; numerical equivalence does not establish equivalent control or harm.

links.label: Wikipedia

IAEA 2010: linear-quadratic parameter, repair and time assumptions, section 3.12.7

notes: For equal brief external-beam fractions, the basic linear-quadratic expression is BED = n × d × [1 + d/(alpha/beta)]. Here n is the count, d is dose per fraction in gray and alpha/beta is a tissue-and-endpoint parameter in gray, so the ratio inside the bracket is dimensionless. The simplified expression assumes negligible repair during delivery and complete repair between fractions, and omits overall time and repopulation. Prolonged or internally distributed irradiation needs additional modelling; this expression does not automatically compare every brachytherapy or radioligand pattern.

Two invented patterns, fifteen fractions of two gray and five of six gray, each total thirty gray. At an assumed alpha/beta of three gray, their BED values are fifty and ninety gray; at an assumed ten gray, they are 36 and 48. The between-pattern difference is forty under the first assumption and twelve under the second. These assumed parameters are not measurements of a person's cancer or organs. Lower alpha/beta gives fraction size more weight at fixed total dose; a low-ratio tumour narrows a contrast inferred using a ten-gray tumour assumption.

Higher calculated BED means a larger modelled effect under the stated column's assumptions, rather than an observed benefit or toxicity probability. Dose distribution, exposed volume, intervals, overall duration, other exposures, population, comparator, endpoint and follow-up remain necessary. Arithmetic cannot validate extrapolation to a fraction size or settle parameter uncertainty. Five sessions do not identify stereotactic delivery, and this equation measures neither priming nor an abscopal response or immune threshold.

records.name: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) and the full transcriptome
records.tldr: Bulk RNA sequencing measures captured messages pooled across a tissue sample, including contributions from multiple cell types.
records.summary: RNA carries cellular messages; bulk sequencing samples those messages from combined tissue after protocol-specific capture and preparation. Analysis assigns usable observations to genes or transcripts and applies a defined comparison scale. A change can reflect cell composition, expression within cells or both. Gene totals can conceal transcript differences, and pooled RNA does not directly establish protein localisation, pathway flux or drug dependence.

Name the counting unit and normalisation denominator. Estimated transcript counts, length-adjusted transcripts per million and tagged molecule counts answer different measurement questions. A gene total can conceal splice products; pooled RNA does not directly measure surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence. Sources: https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/file_formats.html and https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-0881-8.

Fictional mixture exercise: in two 100-cell samples, increasing identical marker-producing lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles their stipulated marker molecules if each contributes one and other cells contribute none. This does not show cancer-cell activation. Equal RNA contribution and matched recovery are assumptions, not measured tissue properties.
Bulk RNA-seq extracts RNA, prepares a library (often cDNA), may select mRNA or deplete rRNA or capture regions; bulk does not mean equal capture of all molecules.
Reads or fragments are assigned to genes or transcripts; shared sequences make assignment ambiguous; a count table is already shaped by preparation and analysis.
A bulk signal can rise because more cells of a type contribute, expression within them rises, or both; deconvolution estimates contributions under a model and does not separate cells.
Gene-level counts can hide isoform differences; a mutant or splice product needs sequence or junction evidence.

Bulk RNA can nominate expressed targets and summarise programmes but does not establish cell origin, surface protein, pathway flux or drug dependence; zero reads is not absence; thousands of genes from one biopsy are not thousands of patients.

Fictional teaching exercise: With equal RNA per cell, a lymphocyte-only marker and 100-cell pieces, raising lymphocytes from 20 to 40 doubles the pooled marker (20 to 40 stipulated molecules) without changing any cancer cell.
Record sampled region and RNA integrity; research profiling differs from a validated clinical RNA test.

Record protocol-compatible preservation, sampled region, RNA integrity and material consumed by extraction. Track capture, sequence assignment, read/fragment units, normalisation and transcript calls. Preparation time varies; reference material, process controls and biological replicates test different uncertainties. Degradation, contamination, ambiguous annotation, batch and mixture shifts constrain purpose-specific cutoffs and clinical intended-use validation.

records.name: The cancer-immunity cycle
records.tldr: The cancer-immunity cycle maps linked steps from available tumour antigens to T-cell recognition and killing. It helps locate a question or bottleneck; a result at one step does not establish the whole response.
records.summary:
Chen and Mellman’s 2013 framework describes seven linked steps: release of cancer antigens; their collection and presentation; T-cell priming and activation; trafficking; entry into tumour tissue; recognition of cancer cells; and killing. Further antigen release may support another round. In conventional T-cell recognition, a displayed peptide-HLA complex and a suitable T-cell receptor are separate dependencies.

This is a T-cell-centred organizing model, not a universal route, assay result or treatment-selection algorithm. Steps overlap, priming may occur away from the tumour, and other immune mechanisms require their own account. Checkpoints and local tissue conditions affect several steps. Vaccines aim to generate or expand reactive responses, checkpoint drugs interrupt selected inhibitory signals, and engineered cells provide a recognition system and effectors. Each still needs appropriate targets, access, function and safety evidence.

notes: In a fictional vaccine study, blood cells release a cytokine after added-peptide stimulation. This supports reactivity under that assay’s conditions. Added peptide can bypass natural processing, and the result does not establish entry into the sampled tumour, recognition of naturally presenting cancer cells, useful killing or clinical benefit. Antigen release is not priming, blood expansion is not infiltration, and a return arrow does not demonstrate durable protection.

Use the cycle to name the measured step and the next untested dependency. A proposed bottleneck or complementary pair of mechanisms does not establish a beneficial or safe combination. Increasing a response can also affect healthy tissue; the model does not identify a safe intervention by itself.

For a coding change to supply a conventional T-cell target, its information must be expressed, protein produced and processed into a fragment, that peptide displayed with HLA, and a suitable receptor able to recognise the display. DNA, RNA, protein, recovered displayed peptide and controlled recognition are separate observations. A prediction at one step does not measure all the others. This conventional alpha-beta route does not describe every T cell, antibody or natural killer recognition system.

An immune observation suggests a question ladder: identify the cells and their location; ask whether a proposed peptide is produced and displayed; test recognition against appropriate target and background controls; distinguish tissue entry from useful target-specific function; then seek clinical comparisons for benefit and harm. Poor display, few matching cells, failed tissue access and impaired local function are different proposed failures. A count, supplied-peptide response or plausible pathway alone cannot complete that chain. These are task-dependent interpretation questions, not a mandatory clinical test menu.

In an invented vaccine report, one blood clonotype becomes more frequent, its sequence also appears in sampled tumour, a separately tested cell mixture responds to added peptide, and ctDNA becomes undetectable. These are four observations, not proof that this clone killed the cancer. Link the responding cells to a compatible paired receptor, test natural tumour recognition and target death, and preserve each assay's denominator and detection limit. Surgery, chemotherapy, shedding and sampling can also affect ctDNA. Conversely, an unchanged blood repertoire does not exclude a response in unsampled tissue. Temporal coincidence does not establish the causal contribution of one clone.
records.analogy: A relay helps organize the questions: material must be available, presented, recognized and acted on. Several dependencies can be impaired together, and improving one handoff does not establish completion of the response. The map does not predict which treatment will help an individual.
interventions: Radiation, chemotherapy, viruses and antibody-drug conjugates can cause cancer-cell death. Antigen release alone does not establish immunogenic cell death or a useful T-cell response.
Vaccines and antigen-presenting-cell approaches investigate antigen presentation and priming. The framework locates proposed jobs; it does not establish that a particular intervention completes them.
Vascular, chemokine and stromal interventions investigate trafficking or tissue entry in defined systems. Model-specific findings do not establish a general conversion of excluded tumours.

Receptor-engineered cells and engagers change recognition requirements but still depend on accessible targets and functional cells. Conventional TCR recognition remains peptide-HLA-dependent; checkpoint blockade addresses selected inhibitory signals rather than every step.

records.name: Case report
records.tldr: A case report describes what happened to one person or a few, which can reveal a signal or a harm but cannot show what would have happened under a different treatment.
records.summary: A case report documents a clinical course, interventions, outcomes and alternative explanations. It can reveal a signal of benefit or harm without establishing what would have happened under another approach. The CARE reporting guideline includes a timeline, diagnostic assessment, interventions, follow-up, the patient perspective and consent; complete reporting supports appraisal rather than proving treatment causation.

links.label: CARE guidelines: consensus-based clinical case reporting guideline (Deutsches Arzteblatt 2013)

notes: A careful case timeline can preserve an unusual experience and generate questions. Published memorable successes do not supply all treated people as a denominator, so they cannot establish a response probability or treatment ranking. Several scans in one person remain observations from one person. A report usually lacks the concurrent counterfactual outcome under another treatment, and even a rigorous individual comparison would not establish the average effect in everyone sharing a cancer label.

Fictional clinical history: treatment A starts, a procedure is added, treatment B starts and a later scan improves. This establishes improvement during that course, not the separate added contributions of the procedure or B. The earlier treatment, procedure and later treatment can have overlapping lasting influences. Drawing overlapping ribbons represents that possibility and ordering only; it supplies no measured effect size or known duration. Documenting experience and planning an interpretable comparison are different routes to evidence.

A testimonial remains an attributed report until its underlying observations can be checked. In an explicitly fictional blog, a person with metastatic cancer adds an off-label medicine to standard chemotherapy and later scans show shrinkage. Accepting those observations as the example's premise establishes improvement during that combination; it does not isolate the added medicine, its safety or how often the result occurs. Record every intervention and measurement on the timeline and ask for a series or trial with all treated participants, failures, follow-up and a suitable comparison. A company video showing three successes has a different meaning if three of five or three of 500 people were treated. Selected successes do not supply the missing denominator or a personal forecast.

records.name: Cell composition confound (tumour versus stroma and immune cells)
records.tldr: Because a tumour sample is a mix of cancer, stromal and immune cells, a difference between two samples may only reflect a different mix of cells.
records.summary:
A tumour specimen can contain malignant, immune, stromal and normal cells. A difference in an aggregate molecular signal can reflect a changed mixture, changed expression within cells or both. That is different from a directly counted cell fraction or a density per sampled area, each of which also needs its denominator and sampled region.

Preparation can change what is recovered. Slyper and colleagues compared single-cell and single-nucleus profiling in matched tumour specimens and found similar cell types at sometimes different proportions. A recovered profile mixture is therefore not automatically the original tissue census. Deconvolution and purity models can help investigate contributions under assumptions; they do not certify the cell of origin of every signal or remove sampling differences.

notes: In a fictional assay using equal sampled areas and the same counting method, ten immune cells among fifty total cells is 20%, while ten among twenty is 50%. The immune count remains ten. Loss of other cells can raise the fraction without additional immune-cell entry; these observations alone do not establish recruitment, recognition or killing. This simple cell fraction is not the clinical stromal tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte score, which has a different denominator.

A second invented comparison starts with ten cells in one square millimetre of viable edge from lesion L. Follow-up A counts ten in the same stated area and region of L, giving ten cells per square millimetre at both times under the supplied assumptions. Follow-up B counts ten in 0.2 square millimetres from an injured centre of lesion M, giving fifty per square millimetre. B does not show a rise within L. Retain the lesion, viable area, centre or edge, collection time, treatment context and counting method. An early sample can capture transient injury signals and a later one a changed surviving-cell mixture. Equal area does not make separate tissue pieces identical, and matched sampling alone still cannot establish recruitment causation.

Measurement layers ask different questions. Anatomical imaging describes structure; tracer imaging depends on the stated product and its distribution; immunohistochemistry localises a protein in sampled tissue; bulk RNA pools captured messages; receptor sequencing describes recovered sequences and their sampled abundances; and controlled recognition or killing assays test a specified function under their conditions. RNA abundance is not accessible surface protein. Formenti's lung-cancer radiation-plus-ipilimumab study used clinical, blood-repertoire and selected functional readouts together; none is a universal immune-success marker or a substitute for the other measurements.

records.name: cGAS-STING innate sensing
records.tldr: cGAS is a DNA sensor that can activate signalling through STING. The measured signal and immune outcome depend on the cell and context.
records.summary:
Sensor and messenger are separate steps: in cell experiments cGAS bound DNA in the cytoplasm and made the second messenger cGAMP, which binds and activates STING (Sun et al., 2013), and the presence of DNA does not by itself measure cGAS activity.

STING normally sits in the endoplasmic reticulum; in the cells tested it moved to perinuclear compartments on activation, and palmitoylation at the Golgi was essential for activation (Mukai et al., 2016). That is intracellular trafficking, not release of STING as a circulating messenger.

The consequence depends on the cell. Host STING was needed for spontaneous CD8 T-cell priming against tumours in mice (Woo et al., 2014). In chromosomally unstable tumour models, ruptured micronuclei spilled DNA into the cytosol and activated cGAS and STING, and continuing chromosome segregation errors promoted invasion and metastasis in a STING-dependent manner (Bakhoum et al., 2018). A later study reported interferon tachyphylaxis and an endoplasmic reticulum stress response downstream of chronic STING activation in such cells, and an association of chromosomal instability and cGAS activation in micronuclei with immune suppression and metastasis in human triple-negative breast cancer (Li et al., 2023). An interferon RNA signal in a tumour sample cannot identify the producing cell or the sensor behind it, and acute and repeated stimulation can differ, which is not a rule that short stimulation helps and long stimulation harms.

records.name: Cross-trial comparison
records.tldr: Results from separate studies can differ because the people, care or measurements differ. Comparing their headline percentages does not by itself show which treatment works better.
records.summary: A comparison between separate studies must account for differences in participants, treatment, background care, endpoints, clocks and follow-up. Randomisation protects the comparison within a trial; it does not randomise participants between unrelated trials. Formal indirect comparisons can retain within-trial contrasts through a common comparator, but depend on compatible effect modifiers and methods. A higher headline percentage in one study is insufficient to rank treatments.

notes: A higher percentage in one paper is a reason to examine its study, rather than proof that its treatment is better. Randomisation protects comparisons within a trial, not between separately conducted trials. Comparing their experimental arms discards that protection. Disease burden, biomarker assay and threshold, prior treatment, background care, dose, endpoint rules, analysis population and follow-up can differ. Formal indirect comparison through a common comparator preserves each trial's treatment-versus-control contrast but still requires compatible questions and methods. Pooling active arms across trials is prone to bias, and even an adjusted indirect estimate remains less secure than a suitable direct comparison (Bucher and colleagues, 1997). Network meta-analysis adds a transitivity assumption: important effect modifiers must be sufficiently comparable across the network. A shared drug name or statistical agreement cannot establish that unmeasured compatibility. Similar endpoint labels can hide different definitions: a clinical benefit rate may include different durations of stable disease. Adjustment for measured differences does not remove every bias, and lower hazard ratios against different comparators cannot automatically rank treatments.

Two fictional single-arm studies each enrol 100 people with the same response definition, assessment period and complete denominator. In the favourable baseline group, A has 40 responses among 80 people (50%) and B has 12 among 20 (60%). In the other group, A has 4/20 (20%) and B 24/80 (30%). Overall, A has 44% response and B 36%, despite B's higher rate in both groups. A enrolled an 80/20 mixture of the two groups, while B enrolled 20/80. Composition reverses the headline ranking. This arithmetic does not establish that B is superior: people were not randomised between studies, and one measured feature cannot resolve every difference.

A fictional vaccine report of 90% recurrence-free at two years in selected postoperative patients cannot be ranked against 30% objective response in a different advanced-disease drug study. Immune response, pathological response, imaging response and survival are different outcomes in different settings. A comparative effect estimate needs a shared clinical question and defensible design. For time-to-event results, align the event definition, origin, assessment schedule, cutoff and follow-up as well as population and care. FDA's December 2018 endpoint guidance warns that external survival comparisons can reflect selection, imaging and supportive-care differences. Neither fictional example certifies an actual indirect comparison.

records.name: Cryoablation
records.tldr: Cryoablation extracts heat through an applicator to freeze selected tissue. A visible ice ball does not show that every point received lethal exposure.
records.summary:
Freezing and thawing can injure cells through ice formation, osmotic changes and vascular injury. The historical mechanistic literature emphasises temperature, time, thawing and repetition; a probe setpoint is not exposure everywhere in the tissue. The visible frozen region and the lethal boundary need separate assessment.

Georgiades and colleagues studied normal renal tissue in swine. Measurements from six test animals found a mean nonlethal rim of 0.75 millimetres, with variation and widening near large vessels. Their proposed six-millimetre visible-ice margin for renal cancer was an extrapolation under stated assumptions, rather than a measured universal human margin.

Site, geometry, applicators and nearby structures affect feasibility and harm. Freezing, preserved material or local tissue destruction alone does not establish antigen presentation, useful immune priming or distant tumour control.

records.name: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)
records.tldr: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) consists of fragments of DNA shed by tumour cells into the blood, detectable with sensitive sequencing.
records.summary: Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) is made up of DNA fragments shed by tumour cells into the bloodstream, where they form only a small fraction of all cell-free DNA and are detected with sensitive sequencing. Its uses span genotyping for companion diagnostics, tracking resistance mutations such as EGFR T790M and ESR1, molecular residual disease, early detection and response monitoring. Shedding varies with tumour type and burden, and clonal haematopoiesis can confound results. The term underpins the Liquid biopsy (ctDNA), MRD / molecular residual disease testing and Multi-cancer early detection (MCED) technologies, and it appears in the SERENA-6, CIRCULATE-Japan and IMvigor011 trials and in ideas on molecular-progression switching beyond ESR1 and HPV ctDNA to guide cervical cancer therapy.

notes: Detection depends on stage and tumour type: with digital PCR-based methods in 640 patients, ctDNA was found in more than 75% of people with advanced pancreatic, ovarian, colorectal, bladder, gastro-oesophageal, breast, melanoma, hepatocellular and head and neck cancers, and in fewer than 50% of primary brain, renal, prostate or thyroid cancers. In localised disease it was found in 73% of colorectal, 57% of gastro-oesophageal, 48% of pancreatic and 50% of breast adenocarcinomas, and it was often present in people with no detectable circulating tumour cells (Bettegowda 2014). The assay, specimen and population are part of each figure.

ctDNA is a subset of cell-free DNA, and not every plasma variant is tumour-derived: in paired plasma and white-blood-cell sequencing, 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 people without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis (Razavi 2019). A ctDNA result is also a quantity with a unit (molecules per millilitre, a fraction, or a call), and the same number means different things under each.

Lung cancer: plasma genotyping at diagnosis is non-inferior to tissue for finding a guideline biomarker (27.3% against 21.3% in 282 patients), has 100% positive predictive value for the alterations with approved drugs, returns in 9 days against 15, and raises detection by 48% when added to tissue (Leighl 2019). Clinical sensitivity against tissue is 80%, so a negative plasma result rules nothing out and the guideline permits plasma to rule in only (Lindeman 2018). Serial plasma after starting treatment also separates the patients whose resistant clone was already present, within three weeks (Oxnard 2018).

records.name: DNA
records.tldr: DNA stores sequence information. Its packaging, copying and use as a template for RNA are different processes.
records.summary: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.

records.name: Hypofractionation (fewer, larger radiotherapy doses)
records.tldr: Hypofractionation uses larger radiation doses per treatment than a specified comparison schedule, usually with fewer treatments. Control and harms depend on the whole tested regimen.
records.summary:
Hypofractionation uses larger doses per fraction relative to a stated conventional comparison, commonly with fewer treatments. Keep total gray, dose per fraction, count, spacing, overall duration and treatment volume together. For equal fractions, total physical dose is the fraction count multiplied by dose per fraction; this arithmetic does not establish biological equivalence. Acceleration changes overall timing; a boost changes the dose to a selected region. Hypofractionation does not by itself identify stereotactic delivery.

Biological response depends on tissue, repair and timing, rather than total physical dose alone. Alpha/beta is a model parameter in gray describing fraction-size sensitivity. Under the linear-quadratic model and its assumptions, a lower ratio predicts greater sensitivity to fraction size at the same total physical dose. Historical teaching values near 10 gray for early effects and 3 for late effects are conventions, not universal constants. A planned START-A/pilot meta-analysis estimated 4.6 gray for tumour control, with confidence interval 1.1 to 8.1, and 3.4 for late photographic breast change, with interval 2.3 to 4.5. Keep the model, endpoint and uncertainty.

START-B compared 50 gray in 25 fractions over five weeks with 40 in 15 over three weeks after surgery for early breast cancer, assessing local-regional relapse and late effects. FAST-Forward tested 40 gray in 15 fractions over three weeks against 27 or 26 in five over one week to the whole breast or chest wall. Its five-year report supported non-inferiority of 26 gray for breast relapse under the trial margin; 27 gray produced more normal-tissue effects. These results do not validate every five-visit course, nodal field, reirradiation plan or immune-priming schedule.

records.name: Immunohistochemistry (IHC)
records.tldr: Staining a tissue slice with antibodies so a protein shows up in colour under the microscope.
records.summary: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) uses antibody binding and signal development to show a selected protein in a prepared tissue section. Interpretation retains which cells and compartments stain, the intensity and distribution, and the named marker-specific method. A percentage, intensity category or composite score can describe different aspects of the result. Fixation, retrieval, controls, sampling and observer variation affect interpretation. Automated quantification also needs validation for its marker, specimens and intended use. A research stain or generic score does not replace a validated clinical selection assay.

notes: There is no universal IHC scoring scale or positivity threshold. Retain antibody clone, retrieval and detection method, controls, eligible cells, subcellular location, intensity, distribution and intended use. A research stain does not automatically replace a clinical selection assay.

An H-score under the intensity-weighted convention is weak-cell percentage plus twice moderate-cell percentage plus three times strong-cell percentage, on a 0 to 300 scale. Fictional example: 50 unstained, 10 weak, 20 moderate and 20 strong cells out of 100 give 50% positive and H-score 110. Neither is a molecule count.

Bulk receptor abundance and staining mainly on blood vessels can both be correct: one measures a mixture and the other locates signal. Neither establishes target accessibility or treatment benefit. Staining also does not establish protein activity or cancer-cell dependence on that protein.

IHC makes selected proteins visible through antibody binding and signal development in a prepared section. Specificity, retrieval, detection, positive controls, internal controls and background matter. Nuclear and membrane signals answer different questions. Multiplex fluorescence adds markers but still needs validated antibody performance and cell-boundary assignment.

In the conventional Allred scheme, proportion categories are 0 for no positive cells, 1 for less than 1%, 2 for 1% to 10%, 3 for 11% to 33%, 4 for 34% to 66% and 5 for 67% to 100%. Intensity is 0 for absent staining or 1, 2 and 3 for weak, moderate and strong staining. The total is 0 or 2 to 8. In a fictional separate example, 30% positive cells with moderate staining give 3 + 2 = 5. These integer bins are a named convention, not a universal positivity rule.

Equal H-scores can conceal different intensity distributions. A negative clinical category does not establish zero protein molecules. HER2 and hormone-receptor assays have marker-specific reporting rules; current CAP breast reporting retains percentage and intensity even when an optional composite score is given.

A useful IHC result identifies the block, fixation and section, antibody clone, retrieval and detection system, eligible cells and scored compartment. Cutting and staining use finite tissue. Report the percentage, intensity, location and named scoring scale, together with expected-positive tissue, relevant internal controls and background assessment. Poor preservation, nonspecific binding, few eligible cells, heterogeneous staining and observer variation can limit interpretation. Validation must fit the assay and its intended use; a research measurement is not automatically a clinical selection test.

records.name: Immuno-PET
records.tldr: Immuno-PET uses a radiolabelled antibody or an antibody-derived binder to image its distribution. Uptake depends on access, binding and clearance as well as the target; clinical usefulness needs separate evidence.
records.summary:
Immuno-PET uses radiolabelled antibodies or antibody-derived binders. Full immunoglobulin G (IgG), antigen-binding fragments (Fab), minibodies and single-domain nanobodies differ in size and pharmacokinetics. The format can affect penetration, clearance, retention and normal-organ background; there is no universal best format. A label makes the binder traceable, not a perfect detector of every target site.

The radionuclide must suit the product's imaging time course. Dijkers' 89Zr-trastuzumab study examined a full antibody over several days; Keyaerts' 68Ga-HER2 nanobody study imaged at earlier times. These are product-specific examples. Antibody imaging can concern a tumour-associated target or immune cells. CD8 binder imaging belongs here; granzyme-B peptide or peptidomimetic imaging is a different tracer class and has its own record.

notes: Imagine sending a labelled binding tool into the body. Some remains in blood, some reaches accessible sites, and some fails to bind or clears. Delivery, access, target binding, competition, clearance and retention all affect the image. Therapeutic or unlabelled antibody can compete for the same target or alter distribution and background. A smaller signal after same-target treatment is therefore not, by itself, target loss. A conceptual labelled/unlabelled-binder drawing supplies these alternatives, not uptake values.

Dijkers and colleagues studied 14 people with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer using 89Zr-trastuzumab, with different antibody masses and scan times. The study addressed feasibility, biodistribution and visualisation, not universal treatment selection. Keyaerts and colleagues studied 20 women with primary or metastatic breast cancer scored HER2 IHC 2+ or 3+ using a 68Ga-HER2 nanobody in a phase 1 safety, distribution and dosimetry study. Tumour targeting and no observed adverse reactions in that small study do not establish general safety, individual benefit or an interchangeable imaging schedule.

Bensch and colleagues imaged 22 patients across three tumour types with 89Zr-atezolizumab before PD-L1 blockade. Uptake varied within and between patients and included high signal in lymphoid tissues and inflammation. Associations with treatment response were exploratory. Imaging an accessible PD-L1-associated distribution does not isolate malignant cells, convert uptake into an expression percentage or prove that a scan-directed treatment choice improves outcomes.

CD8 imaging traces a labelled CD8-binding construct, not the total number of tumour-killing cells. Farwell's phase 1 study included 15 patients: tumour uptake appeared in 10, including 7 of 8 receiving immunotherapy. Lymphoid and normal-organ distribution were also part of the observation. The paper appeared online in 2021 and in print in 2022. Kist de Ruijter's 38-person phase 1/2 study found heterogeneous 89Zr-CD8 tracer uptake, associations with tissue CD8 and inflamed versus desert patterns, and an exploratory association between higher baseline uptake and survival. On-treatment lesion-uptake changes did not simply track response. These mixed-cancer studies do not establish antigen recognition, cell killing or a validated stop/switch strategy for breast cancer.

An interpretable tracer record retains the exact binder and format, isotope, protein mass in micrograms or mg, administered activity in MBq and time after injection. Background in blood and normal organs, lesion size and clearance affect interpretation. One image cannot isolate every delivery, binding and retention contribution, quantify receptor occupancy or supply a therapeutic absorbed dose. Protein mass is not a target-positive cell fraction, and uptake is not an expression percentage.

In a fictional course, uptake is lower after an antibody against the same target. Before declaring that the target disappeared, compare tracer and therapeutic exposure, labelled and unlabelled mass, image timing, blood background, delivery, access and clearance. Competition is one explanation among several. A controlled binding experiment or suitable sampled tissue would answer a different, more specific question, each with its own limits. The image alone neither assigns all signal to cancer nor chooses a treatment.

strengths: Images target and immune infiltrate non-invasively

records.name: Immunogenic cell death
records.tldr: Immunogenic cell death is regulated cell death that can initiate adaptive immunity against the dying cells in a suitable host and context. Injury alone does not establish it.
records.summary:
The 2020 consensus defines immunogenic cell death through the adaptive immune response, not merely the appearance of dead cells. Antigens, appropriately timed danger signals, antigen-presenting cells and a responsive host all matter. Apoptotic or other death machinery does not by itself classify the immune outcome.

Calreticulin exposure, ATP or HMGB1 release and interferon-related signals are useful mechanistic readouts, but none alone proves protective immunity. Functional cross-priming and appropriate in-vivo immune tests address later steps. The consensus distinguishes mouse vaccination models from established disease; neither a surrogate marker nor a positive mouse assay establishes clinical benefit in a person.

notes: In a local-treatment study, follow injury and signals through presentation, priming, recognition and measured tumour outcomes. Circulating cytokines or proliferating T cells alone do not establish tumour-specific killing, distant control or an optimal radiation dose.

Immunogenic cell death is regulated death capable of initiating antigen-specific adaptive immunity in a compatible responding host. Antigenicity and appropriately timed adjuvant signals are both necessary considerations. It is an immune consequence, not an exclusive machine opposed to apoptosis or necrotic appearance.

Surface calreticulin, released ATP and HMGB1 have distinct mechanistic roles in defined experiments. Calreticulin supported dying-cell uptake, ATP signalled through dendritic-cell P2X7/inflammasome pathways, and HMGB1/TLR4 supported processing and presentation. These are examples rather than a universal sufficient three-marker checklist. A DAMP is not automatically a tumour-specific antigen.

In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Compare later challenge with living matched tumour cells in vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts, and test specificity with unrelated compatible tumour cells. Incidence and growth are functional readouts. Immune-competent versus deficient comparisons alone cannot isolate immunogenic death from other immunostimulation. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Residual inducer, contamination, incompatible antigens and poor death confirmation can invalidate attribution. No universal DAMP cutoff establishes immunogenicity.

Death plus extracellular ATP does not establish a cancer vaccine. Danger signals, cross-priming, functional protection, distant control and patient benefit are separate claims. Even a positive mouse vaccination assay remains model-bound and does not select a clinical treatment.

records.name: In situ vaccination
records.tldr: In situ vaccination aims to use antigens at a tumour site to stimulate useful immune recognition. Local destruction does not automatically make the tumour a successful vaccine.
records.summary:
Local treatment can supply tumour antigens, and an adjuvant or other immune intervention may support their presentation and priming. The proposal needs evidence for each step and for useful immune effects in the relevant host and setting. It does not guarantee recognition of every antigen or every lesion.

Injury, danger signals, immune-cell changes, distant lesion responses and comparative patient outcomes are different observations. The actual local method and accompanying treatments must be named. A response during combined treatment does not isolate which component caused it.

notes: The strategy uses relevant tumour antigens in place while supporting presenting cells and immune activation. Antigen availability, uptake and processing, cross-presentation, suitable priming, access to another lesion, recognition of naturally displayed targets and useful function are conditional jobs. Local injury can supply material without establishing all these steps, and danger signals alone do not establish immunogenic cell death. An uninjected lesion can still be exposed to systemic drugs.

Intratumoral immunotherapy describes a delivery route and treatment purpose; in-situ vaccination describes a proposed learning strategy. Not every injected cytotoxic or immune-directed treatment is a vaccine. Local shrinkage, antigen-reactive blood responses, distant control and longer-term clinical benefit are different outcomes, and a multicomponent result does not isolate each component’s contribution.

Brody’s early study combined low-dose radiation and an injected CpG TLR9 agonist in 15 people with low-grade B-cell lymphoma. Hammerich combined Flt3 ligand, radiation and the TLR3 agonist poly-ICLC in indolent lymphoma with accompanying models. The latter report’s restored sensitivity to PD-1 blockade was demonstrated in mice; it is not established human combination benefit or evidence for every injection or a breast-cancer regimen.

Assessment combines local sampling, controlled immune assays and serial treated/uninjected-lesion measurements. Tissue, blood and viable cells are finite inputs. Keep local change, specified reactive-cell counts or functions, and response proportions under their stated rules separate. No universal marker proves successful vaccination. Nonspecific inflammation, added peptide, viability, missed sampling times and concurrent therapy can confound results; a model or assay needs separate clinical validation of the complete intervention.

Added peptide can bypass natural processing. Appropriate naturally presenting targets and recognition or cytotoxicity controls address a separate bridge, within the model’s limits. In a fictional study, the injected lesion shrinks and blood cells respond to supplied tumour peptides, while another lesion is unchanged. Local activity and assay reactivity were observed; natural recognition, access and useful distant function remain unproven. The unchanged lesion also does not establish absence of every immune-learning event.

For T-cell-directed therapeutic strategies, compare the antigen source and what can be selected beforehand. An in-situ approach uses tumour material in the body and selects a site and intervention; a supplied design selects planned composition or encoded targets using adequate sample information or material. Defined peptide or encoded targets differ from broader cell preparations. Manufacturing a product does not mean every peptide ultimately displayed is known or controlled. The room-material versus teaching-kit analogy describes these inputs, not assured learning or a winner.

Priming is initial activation of a naive T cell. Cross-presentation places externally acquired material on class I HLA in a presenting cell; that event is distinct from a cancer cell naturally displaying a recognised target. Both strategies still need evidence of presentation, suitable priming or expansion, tumour access, useful function, outcomes and harms. Dashed links in a comparison diagram mark questions to investigate, not successful completion of each step.

The required opportunity depends on the method. A lesion-based local approach needs available tumour material at an identified, safely accessible site. A supplied product needs appropriate information or material and a workable manufacturing and delivery plan. If no identifiable lesion is accessible, that removes the stated opportunity for that local method; it does not show that another vaccine is feasible or choose treatment. Match a research question about local material and support to that design, or one about planned antigen selection to a supplied design, then compare complete strategies in suitable studies.

Injection specifies a route, and using one person's tumour material is not equivalent to manufacturing a selected personalised vaccine. A study can combine local tumour material with a supplied antigen product; report both sources rather than forcing one exclusive category. Personalisation, platform and route are independent descriptors. Local shrinkage, an immune assay and control at another lesion remain different outcomes.

Consider two fictional cards. A uses accessible tumour material with a local intervention and immune stimulus; B supplies selected encoded targets based on sample information. Neither gives outcome data. A does not specify a fixed presented mixture, and B does not guarantee processing, HLA display or natural tumour recognition. For both, investigate presentation, priming, access and function and then matched clinical outcomes and harms. If A's lesion becomes inaccessible, B is not thereby chosen. If B is added to A, the study now uses both antigen sources.

The examples answer different questions. Brody used radiation plus injected CpG in low-grade lymphoma. Hammerich used Flt3 ligand, low-dose radiation and poly-ICLC in indolent lymphoma, with accompanying models; the reported new responsiveness to PD-1 blockade was in mice. Ott's melanoma study supplied selected long peptides with poly-ICLC. These are not a head-to-head efficacy ranking, evidence for a breast-cancer regimen or an individual eligibility assessment.

strengths: Can investigate tumour-derived antigens without preselecting every sequence

limitations: Local injury or marker release does not establish protective immunity
Access and delivery requirements depend on the chosen method

records.name: Intratumoral immunotherapy
records.tldr: Intratumoral immunotherapy delivers an immune-directed treatment within a tumour. Local effects, immune responses and control of other lesions need separate evidence.
records.summary:
Intratumoral describes a route into a tumour, while immunotherapy describes the intended immune-directed action. Products, injection methods and accompanying treatments differ. A lesion-based method needs an identified safely accessible site; local delivery does not guarantee confined exposure or systemic safety.

An in-situ vaccination strategy is one possible use of local tumour material, rather than a synonym for every injection. Evidence must distinguish injected-lesion changes, controlled immune assays, uninjected-lesion outcomes and the whole regimen’s benefits and harms.

notes: Intratumoral means within a tumour; intralesional means within a lesion. Intratumoral immunotherapy combines a route with an immune-directed treatment purpose. The name does not identify the substance, and a locally injected cytotoxic drug need not be immunotherapy. An in-situ vaccination strategy seeks useful immune learning from material in the body; it is not a synonym for every injection. Local-material and learning analogies leave direct drug effects and procedure risks unresolved.

A lesion-based injection needs an identified site that can be reached safely by the specified method. The accessible lesion may not represent every other tumour site. Entry of a needle does not establish uniform distribution, confined exposure or systemic safety. Recruitment or activation of presenting cells, antigen collection and priming can be investigated, while travel to another lesion, natural recognition and sustained function remain separate questions. Inflammation, local injury, infection and systemic effects depend on the product and procedure.

Hammerich's 2019 report studied a particular strategy in indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma: Flt3 ligand, low-dose radiation and the TLR3 agonist poly-ICLC. NCT01976585 specifies intratumoral Flt3 ligand and poly-ICLC with low-dose radiotherapy. It does not make every injected immune agent the same intervention. Marabelle's 2018 paper is an expert terminology and reporting recommendation, rather than a trial establishing efficacy of the class.

Keep three measurements separate. Changes in size or tissue at the injected lesion show local observations. Controlled assays of antigen-reactive cells ask an immune-response question but leave natural recognition and function elsewhere unresolved. Changes at uninjected lesions ask another question, while the injection's added effect and longer-term patient benefit need a suitable comparison. Report each component's route and serial injected and uninjected lesion results. An uninjected lesion can still receive systemic co-treatment, so it need not be untreated.

The U.S. Imlygic label specifies talimogene laherparepvec for local treatment of unresectable cutaneous, subcutaneous and nodal melanoma lesions recurrent after initial surgery. It states that improved overall survival and an effect on visceral metastases have not been shown. A local melanoma indication does not establish whole-body benefit or a breast-cancer indication. Intralesional administration also does not remove the label's infection, wound and other product-specific precautions.

In a fictional study, the injected lesion shrinks, a controlled immune assay becomes positive and a separate lesion stays unchanged. The observations establish local and assay activity under their stated definitions, without demonstrating distant control. The result also does not establish that no immune-learning event occurred. Testing naturally presenting targets, relevant function, later outcomes and harms addresses additional questions.

For radiation, an abscopal effect describes an observation outside the irradiated field. After an injection, describe an uninjected-lesion response and name concurrent treatments before attributing it to the injection or to immunity. Marabelle's expert panel specifically distinguished injected from noninjected lesions because systemic co-treatment can expose both. A combination's name alone does not reveal which component was injected.

Read the component list before interpreting a combination. Intratumoral means inside a tumour and intravenous means into a vein; an accompanying checkpoint antibody may have either route according to the protocol. Record the injected material and lesion, every systemic drug and its route, and any radiation or ablation. Electroporation uses electrical pulses to support entry into cells; the injected gene payload and electrical delivery are separate intervention components. Track lesions whose injection status changes over time. Product manufacture, dosing procedures, monitoring and subsequent surgery or care belong in the study plan; a registry listing establishes neither benefit, local availability nor eligibility. DCIS, invasive breast cancer and melanoma are different populations, and a preoperative pathological response is not a survival endpoint.

In an invented single-arm study, twelve people each have an injected and an uninjected lesion, and all receive a systemic drug. At the stated assessment, injected-lesion responses occur in eight, uninjected-lesion responses in two and a defined blood immune-assay response in five. Each denominator is twelve, but participants can overlap: adding the counts to claim fifteen responders is invalid. These lesion counts do not provide the target-lesion, non-target and new-lesion information needed for a formal patient response category. Even all three observations in one person would not isolate the injection's contribution. Compare the combination with the same systemic treatment without the injected intervention, retaining population, endpoints, assessment timing, harms and appropriate control or blinding procedures.

records.name: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs)
records.tldr: Checkpoint inhibitors can cause immune-related adverse events such as colitis, rash, hepatitis, pneumonitis and thyroid problems. Management depends on the organ and severity and may involve steroids, other immunosuppression or hormone replacement.
records.summary:
Immune-related adverse events are injuries attributed to treatment-related immune activity, commonly discussed with checkpoint inhibitors. They can affect the bowel, lung, skin, liver, hormone-producing glands and other organs. A symptom or laboratory change during treatment does not by itself establish an immune cause.

Clinical assessment identifies the organ, severity, timing and competing explanations. Reactions can arise after treatment stops, and some endocrine injury leaves lasting loss of function. Organ-specific management can include different measures, such as treatment interruption, immunosuppression or hormone replacement. An adverse event, an attributed immune injury and a cancer-response result are separate findings.

notes: What the label does and does not say. An adverse event is any unfavourable and unintended sign, symptom or abnormal laboratory finding that occurs during treatment, whether or not the treatment caused it; grading records that it occurred and how severe it was, and the clinical team assigns attribution to the drug, the intervention or something else (NCI Cancer Therapy Evaluation Program). An irAE is the narrower attribution of harm to treatment-related immune activity, so a symptom during immunotherapy is not automatically an irAE, and the abbreviation names a suspected mechanism, not an organ, a severity or a treatment. The SITC 2021 guideline uses the same wording, grades events including irAEs on a scale such as CTCAE version 5, and says that some irAEs need organ-specific management while overarching principles apply to all checkpoint-inhibitor toxicity. Checkpoint regulation helps limit responses against healthy tissue, part of peripheral tolerance; disrupting that protection can contribute to immune injury, but no single mechanism explains every event. Colitis names bowel inflammation and pneumonitis lung inflammation. A symptom or the suffix "-itis" does not establish its cause.

Timing and neighbouring syndromes. Immune-mediated reactions to PD-1 or PD-L1 antibodies can occur in any organ system at any time after starting and can also appear after treatment stops (pembrolizumab prescribing information), so the infusion calendar does not define the observation window; onset differs by organ, with a SITC median of 5 to 10 weeks for diarrhoea or colitis and rash typically presenting 2 to 5 weeks after the first treatment. Cytokine release syndrome and ICANS after immune effector cell therapy are separate syndromes with their own ASTCT definitions and grading, not substitute labels for checkpoint-related organ injury, and stopping a treatment does not guarantee the immune effect has stopped.

Report symptoms using the care team's plan and tell evaluating clinicians about current and previous immunotherapy. New or worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain or confusion can need urgent assessment. A person with a new cough after checkpoint treatment should neither dismiss the possible relationship because dosing ended nor infer pneumonitis without evaluation. The organ-inflammation guidance from NCI advises reporting concerning changes rather than waiting for another infusion or starting immune-suppressing treatment independently. Suspected immune injury does not show that the cancer treatment is working.

Pembrolizumab before and after surgery for triple-negative breast cancer: Macmillan says the treatment can make the immune system too active, that side effects can start during treatment or after it ends, and that glands making hormones (such as the thyroid) can be permanently affected, sometimes needing daily tablets. Breast Cancer Now says you should be given an alert card listing the symptoms to report and an out-of-hours contact.

The symptoms both charities ask you to report straight away on the 24-hour number: more stools than usual, stools at night, watery stools or tummy cramps (bowel inflammation); breathlessness, a cough that does not go away, wheeze or fever (lung inflammation); yellow skin or eyes, sickness (liver inflammation); unusual tiredness, headaches that do not go away, dizziness, thirst or passing more urine (hormone glands).

Lung cancer: checkpoint treatment is used at every stage of lung cancer, so the same warning list applies whether it is given before surgery, after chemoradiotherapy or for cancer that has spread. Macmillan says to contact the hospital straight away on the 24-hour number for breathlessness, a cough that does not go away, wheezing or a fever over 37.5 C (lung inflammation); for passing more stools than is normal for you or passing stools at night (bowel inflammation); for a spreading rash, blistering or peeling skin with flu-like symptoms; and for a temperature above 37.5 C or below 36 C or feeling unwell with a normal temperature. It also says these can start during treatment or after treatment ends, which is why the patient alert card is worth carrying.

records.name: The linear-quadratic model and fractionation
records.tldr: A model of radiation response combines a term proportional to dose with one proportional to dose squared. Its use depends on the tissue, endpoint and irradiation pattern.
records.summary:
The linear-quadratic model expresses the surviving cell fraction after dose d as exp(-alpha × d - beta × d squared). The alpha/beta ratio is a parameter in gray for a specified tissue and endpoint. At fixed total physical dose, a lower ratio gives fraction size greater weight. Historical teaching values near ten gray for many tumours and early-responding tissues such as skin and mucosa, and three for late normal-tissue effects, are conventions rather than constants for every tumour or organ. A planned START-A/pilot meta-analysis estimated 4.6 gray for breast tumour control, with 95% confidence interval 1.1 to 8.1, and 3.4 for late photographic breast change, interval 2.3 to 4.5. The trialists interpreted these estimates as similar fraction-size sensitivity for breast cancer and its dose-limiting normal tissues.

The basic equal-fraction calculation assumes equal effects per fraction and complete repair between fractions and does not include overall treatment time. Too short an interval or slow repair can violate that assumption. Extrapolation to a large fraction size or prolonged irradiation needs assessment; a model calculation alone validates neither the pattern nor clinical equivalence.

Relative biological effectiveness rescales the gray before the linear-quadratic formula is applied; a proton plan at RBE 1.1 and the same plan at a variable, LET-weighted RBE are different EQD2 maps.

Explains why hypofractionation works in breast and prostate cancer
limitations: Overestimates kill at very large fractions
Ignores time, hypoxia and immune effects unless extended

records.name: Oligometastatic disease
records.tldr: Oligometastatic disease means a limited number of detected distant metastases under a stated definition. The count alone does not establish all disease is visible or that treating each site will produce a cure.
records.summary:
Oligometastatic disease describes limited detected distant spread, under a specified clinical or study definition. It is a hypothesis that some limited patterns may be amenable to treatment directed at all visible sites; a few visible lesions do not prove a distinct biology or the absence of microscopic disease. Regional lymph nodes alone are not distant metastases.

The ESTRO-ASTRO consensus describes one to five lesions, with every site safely treatable, while acknowledging that there is no universally established maximum. A consensus definition is not proof of added benefit. Treatment decisions require the cancer setting, prior burden and treatment, comparator, endpoint, safety and the person's goals.

notes: A few lit windows show what is detectable, not a census of every room. This analogy does not mean that every limited pattern conceals widespread disease. Synchronous metastases are detected near the initial diagnosis; metachronous metastases are detected later, with the interval defined by the author or protocol. Induced limited disease follows previously widespread disease and systemic treatment. Oligoprogression means a growing subset while other disease remains controlled during treatment. Limited residual or persistent disease means limited visible disease remains after treatment; specify whether it is stable or progressing. These labels are not universal synonyms.

The SABR-COMET randomised phase 2 study enrolled 99 selected patients with different primary cancers, including 18 with breast cancer, a controlled primary and one to five treatable metastases. Its extended follow-up found eight-year overall survival of 27.2% with SABR plus standard care versus 13.6% with standard care alone, with grade 2 or higher acute or late toxicity of 30.3% versus 9.1%. This mixed-cancer result is not a definitive TNBC treatment effect. Control of an irradiated site, delay in progression, survival and symptom relief are different outcomes.

NRG-BR002 tested adding ablation to first-line systemic therapy in breast cancer with at most four metastases, controlled primary disease, at most 12 months of first-line therapy without progression, and all visible sites amenable to SBRT or resection. Of 129 enrolled patients, 125 were eligible for analysis and 79% had HR-positive/HER2-negative disease. In the protocol-specified phase 2 go/no-go analysis with a December 20, 2021 data cutoff, median progression-free survival was 23.0 months without ablation and 19.5 months with it; the hazard ratio was 0.92, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.57 to 1.47 and stratified P = .42. Overall survival did not differ significantly and the study did not proceed to phase 3. This does not supply a definitive effect for every subtype or erase a separate symptom-relief goal.

Classification uses the imaging and its coverage and sensitivity, lesion and organ counts, locations, sizes, dates, previous burden, systemic treatment and response or progression history. A biopsy may be needed to confirm a finding, but classification is not inherently a tumour-consuming molecular assay. Benign mimics, undetected lesions and missing earlier records can mislead. Keep a protocol's count, timing, primary-control and treatability requirements; five lesions is not a cure cutoff and a molecular result does not universally establish this state.

Three fictional histories can each contain two lesions now: two newly detected metastases with no earlier distant disease, two residual lesions after treatment of many, or two growing sites amid many stable sites during therapy. The numeral counts a different subset in each history. Keep the earlier burden and dates rather than merging these groups. A response-selected group and a progression-selected group answer different questions; curative intent is a documented goal whose success needs long-term outcome measurement, not an inference from the current count.

NRG-BR002's accessible NIH author manuscript distinguishes its protocol-specified phase 2 analysis from non-protocol-specified extended follow-up with a September 4, 2025 cutoff. The latter reported median progression-free survival of 23.0 months without ablation versus 29.5 with it, hazard ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.60 to 1.44, and overall-survival hazard ratio 0.94, interval 0.56 to 1.60. These are separate analyses, not interchangeable updates to one median. The indexed abstract reports overall-survival hazard ratio 1.07 and stratified P = .52. Fifty-six of sixty assigned to ablation received SBRT, about 93%; this was not BOOSTER's probe-based comparison. Table 1 has ten triple-negative participants among 125, 8%, and 99 with hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative cancer. The report does not precisely establish every subtype's effect, and confidence intervals crossing one do not prove zero effect. The authors' recommendation against routine use outside trials retains a separate palliation exception.

records.name: Oligoprogression
records.tldr: Oligoprogression means a limited subset of lesions is progressing while other disease remains controlled during treatment. The definition and evidence for adding local treatment depend on the clinical or study setting.
records.summary:
Oligoprogression describes limited progression within otherwise controlled metastatic disease during treatment. It is not restricted to one or two lesions or to targeted pills: the number, imaging rules and prior treatment depend on the definition being used. Oligometastatic disease describes limited detected distant spread, while limited residual disease describes what remains after treatment; retain the earlier burden and whether the remaining lesions are growing.

Treating progressing sites while continuing systemic therapy is a strategy to evaluate, rather than an automatic instruction. CURB tested adding stereotactic body radiation to standard care in lung and breast cohorts with different results. A current lesion count cannot establish benefit, safety or which systemic treatment should continue.

notes: CURB was an open-label randomised phase 2 study after at least first-line systemic treatment, defining oligoprogression as at most five progressive lesions on CT or PET-CT. The prespecified lung cohort had median progression-free survival of 10.0 months with SBRT plus standard care versus 2.2 with standard care, hazard ratio 0.41, 95% confidence interval 0.22 to 0.75. The breast cohort had 4.4 versus 4.2 months, hazard ratio 0.78, interval 0.43 to 1.43. Failure to show a breast-cohort improvement does not establish an exact zero effect or a precise effect in every breast subtype. The intervention, comparator and harms must stay with the population.

In two fictional current scan reports, each maps two lesions. Card A previously had eight before checkpoint treatment and now has two nongrowing residual lesions; card B had two during systemic treatment and now has one growing while the other remains controlled. A poses a limited-residual-disease question and B a limited-progression question. Equal current counts do not make the histories interchangeable or establish trial eligibility, an optimal procedure or a timing rule. BOOSTER studied a response-selected residual lung-cancer setting; CURB selected progression after systemic treatment.

records.name: Preclinical
records.tldr: Evidence from laboratory, animal and computational work used to study mechanisms, activity and safety. It can guide human studies without establishing patient benefit.
records.summary: Preclinical and nonclinical work studies mechanisms, activity, exposure and safety using specified models. Such experiments can occur before or alongside human studies. Evidence that a model responds does not establish a useful treatment for patients. FDA nonclinical requirements depend on the product and context; its published approaches include justified reductions or replacements of animal studies, so a universal two-species requirement is inaccurate.

notes: In-vitro, in-vivo and human-derived describe experimental setting or origin, not validation of treatment in patients. A cell line can test a direct cell effect, while an immune-intact mouse can test selected tissue and immune interactions; neither reproduces every human cancer, prior treatment or physiology. An immune mechanism needs its relevant components represented and functional. Human tissue grown in a dish or grafted into a mouse remains model evidence about that intervention.

Name the intervention, control, outcome and units before counting replication. The biological unit is the entity about which conclusions are sought, such as a donor. The experimental unit receives an independently assigned intervention; the observational unit is measured. A cage assigned together or a preparation treated before being split can make the animals or wells subsamples. More measured cells do not become more assigned mice. Biological and technical replicate labels vary, so inspect sampling, preparation, allocation and measurement. Repeating runs tests consistency without adding donor identities. Analysing correlated subsamples as independent replicates is pseudoreplication.

Fictional design: each of two donors supplies six wells, three control and three treated. The twelve distinct wells receive independent randomized assignments within donor, separate treatment and no mutual influence, while the analysis retains donor nesting. There are twelve assigned wells and two donor sources, not twelve donors. No cell counts or recommended sample size are supplied. If instead a donor preparation is treated before being split, its wells are subsamples of that assignment. Adding cells does not add wells or donors. This distinction follows from the stipulated allocation, not from a universal rule that wells always are independent.

A controlled fictional mouse study in which local treatment changes a distant tumour can support a distant effect in that model. If a controlled immune-cell depletion reduces that effect, it supports a contribution under those tested conditions. Further steps include safely achievable human exposure, relevant target biology, safety and comparative patient outcomes. Mouse tumour volume is not patient survival, and a laboratory effect size or universal model threshold does not establish clinical benefit. A reproducible mechanism can coexist with an impractical or harmful clinical exposure. These are limits on the inference, not a guarantee that any particular model result will translate.

Retain the model or specimen, treatment and comparator, assigned units and subsamples, exclusions, allocation, blinded assessment, timing, dose, readout units and uncertainty. A cell count, cubic-millimetre tumour volume and named assay signal are different measurements. ARRIVE supports appraisal of animal-study reporting rather than proving a conclusion. Exploratory academic experiments and regulatory safety studies have different purposes and requirements. FDA's context-specific nonclinical approaches, including new approach methodologies, do not validate every model for personal treatment selection.

records.name: Publication format and peer-review status
records.tldr: Whether a claim comes from a conference abstract, a preprint or a full journal article tells you how much of the study you can inspect and what review it has had, but not whether the study is valid.
records.summary: Publication format and review status describe what can be inspected and what scrutiny a report has received. A conference abstract, preprint, full article and correction can report different versions of one study. Identify the study and version, read the available methods and match every result to its population, endpoint and data cutoff. Peer review adds scrutiny; it does not establish that every conclusion is correct or independently replicated.
